input.question: Is it still possible to discover new colors?
input.ground_truth: No. The electromagnetic spectrum (light) is very well known and well understood. Basically, every time you look at a rainbow, you are seeing all the possible colors your eyes can see. **Edit:** Colors are defined by their wavelength. There is a continuum of wavelengths (colors) over which our eye responds (the rainbow). Any color you can perceive (or not) is a result of how our brains and eyes process combinations of these wavelengths/colors. Color (wavelength) is a measurable quantity - there are no colors that scientists have not been able to measure.
